todo_crud.idea: A todo list app with user accounts. Users can register and log in. Each user sees only their own todos. Todos have a title, optional description, due date, priority (low/medium/high), and done/undone

api_endpoints.description: Retrieve a paginated list of users, optionally filtered by username search query.
Retrieve details of a specific user by ID.
Create a new user account with username and password.
Update an existing user's information (e.g., username or password).
Delete a user account.
Retrieve a list of tasks for the authenticated user, supporting search by title/description and filters for status and priority.
Retrieve details of a specific task by ID.
Create a new task for the authenticated user.
Update an existing task (title, description, due date, priority, completed flag).
Delete a task.
Register a new user account (alias of POST /users).
Authenticate a user and return a JWT access token.
Populate the database with demo users, tasks, and priority levels.
Return aggregate statistics such as total users, total tasks, and tasks per priority.

features: Allow users to create an account
Allow users to create new tasks
Allow users to log in to their account

user_stories.want: To register for an account
acceptance_criteria: The user can enter a valid username and password to create an account
The user receives a confirmation message after successfully registering
The user is redirected to the login page after registration

user_stories.want: To log in to my account
acceptance_criteria: The user can enter a valid username and password to log in
The user is redirected to the task list page after successful login
The user sees an error message if the login credentials are invalid

user_stories.want: To create a new task
acceptance_criteria: The user can enter a task title and description
The user can select a due date and priority level for the task
The task is added to the user's task list after creation

user_stories.want: To edit an existing task
acceptance_criteria: The user can select a task to edit
The user can update the task title, description, due date, and priority level
The task is updated in the user's task list after editing

user_stories.want: To delete a task
acceptance_criteria: The user can select a task to delete
The task is removed from the user's task list after deletion
The user is prompted to confirm deletion before it is executed

user_stories.want: To mark a task as complete
acceptance_criteria: The user can select a task to mark as complete
The task is updated to show as completed in the user's task list
The user can filter tasks by completion status

user_stories.want: To filter tasks by status and priority
acceptance_criteria: The user can select a filter option (e.g. 'completed', 'high priority')
The task list is updated to show only tasks that match the selected filter
The user can clear the filter to show all tasks

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — to ensure only authorized users can access their task list
non_functional_requirements.pagination: not required — task lists are expected to be small
non_functional_requirements.search: not required — tasks can be filtered by status and priority
non_functional_requirements.file_uploads: no — no file uploads are needed
non_functional_requirements.real_time: no — real-time updates are not necessary

blog_cms.idea: A blog CMS with author and reader roles. Authors write posts with title, content (markdown), tags, and cover image URL. Posts can be saved as draft or published. Readers see all published posts, can f

api_endpoints.description: Populates database with realistic demo data.
Returns aggregate counts and key metrics for the dashboard.
Authenticates a user and returns a JWT token.
Retrieves the profile of the currently authenticated user.
Retrieves a paginated list of all published blog posts, with optional tag filtering.
Retrieves a single published blog post by its ID.
Retrieves a paginated list of posts by a specific author, including drafts for the author themselves.
Creates a new blog post (initially as a draft).
Updates an existing blog post by its ID.
Publishes a draft post, making it visible to readers.
Unpublishes a published post, making it a draft again.
Deletes a blog post by its ID.
Retrieves a list of all available tags.
Creates a new tag (admin/author only).
Deletes a tag (admin/author only).

features: Secure login for authors and role-based access control to ensure authors can only manage their own posts and readers can only view published content.
Authors can create new posts with title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL, and edit existing posts.
Authors can save posts as drafts for later editing and explicitly publish them when ready, making them visible to readers.
Authors can delete their own posts, removing them from the system.
Readers can view a list of all published posts, displaying title, author, date, and tags.
Readers can filter the list of published posts by selecting one or more tags.
Readers can click on a post to view its full content, including rendered markdown, title, author, date, tags, and cover image.

user_stories.want: to create a new blog post
acceptance_criteria: I can input a title, markdown content, tags, and a cover image URL.
The post is saved as a 'draft' by default upon creation.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully created.

user_stories.want: to save a post as a draft
acceptance_criteria: When I save a post, its status is set to 'draft'.
Draft posts are not visible to readers.
I can access and edit my draft posts from my author dashboard.

user_stories.want: to publish a draft post
acceptance_criteria: I can change the status of a draft post to 'published'.
The published post immediately appears in the list of posts visible to readers.
The published post displays its title, my name, the publication date, and its tags.

user_stories.want: to edit an existing post (draft or published)
acceptance_criteria: I can modify the title, content, tags, and cover image URL of any of my posts.
If the post is published, the changes are reflected immediately for readers.
I receive confirmation that my post has been successfully updated.

user_stories.want: to view a list of all published blog posts
acceptance_criteria: I see a list of posts, each displaying its title, author, publication date, and tags.
Only 'published' posts are visible in this list.
The list is ordered by publication date, newest first.

user_stories.want: to filter posts by a specific tag
acceptance_criteria: I can select a tag to filter the post list.
Only posts containing the selected tag are displayed.
The filter can be cleared to show all published posts again.

user_stories.want: to read a full blog post
acceptance_criteria: When I click on a post title, I am taken to a dedicated page for that post.
The full content (markdown rendered), title, author, publication date, and cover image are displayed.
The post's tags are also visible on the individual post page.

non_functional_requirements.authentication: required — Authors need to log in to manage posts; Readers do not need to log in to view posts.
non_functional_requirements.authorization: Authors can only create, edit, delete, and publish their own posts. Readers can only view published posts.

data_entities_detail.description: Stores user authentication and profile information.

data_entities_detail.description: Stores blog post content and metadata.

data_entities_detail.description: Stores categories for blog posts.

acceptance_criteria: There is a clear option to reset a specific counter.

user_stories.want: to delete an existing counter

After confirming deletion, the counter is removed from my list.
The deleted counter is no longer accessible or visible.
